newsitem.title: USA: N.C. man found guilty of killing nine women.
newsitem.headline: N.C. man found guilty of killing nine women.

text.p: Confessed serial killer Henry Wallace was convicted Tuesday of murdering nine women, all co-workers at Charlotte-area fast food restaurants, friends of his sister or friends of a former girlfriend.

Jurors deliberated for more than 15 hours over four days to reach the unanimous verdict on the nine first-degree murder counts. Wallace, 31, was also convicted of eight counts of first-degree rape, one count of second-degree rape, and 11 other charges of robbery, sexual offence and assault.

Prosecutors said they will seek the death penalty in the case in a separate proceeding before the same jury of seven women and five men and the same judge. They will not consider whether Wallace dies for the crimes until next week.
Wallace sat in Mecklenburg County Superior Court between his public defender and his private attorney with hands clasped and stared quietly at the clerk as she read the verdict.
Victims' family members held hands as the verdict was read. One wept openly, another thumbed through a Bible. Later, they hugged each other and prosecutors Marsha Goodenow and Anne Tompkins.

"I still see no remorse," said Vanessa Jumper-Sumter whose sister Valencia was raped, strangled and then set on fire by Wallace. "He didn't even seem upset that they found him guilty of first-degree murder."

Wallace was arrested in March 1994 and gave police taped statements detailing how he had murdered 10 women in Charlotte, most through strangulation after raping them in their homes. Tuesday's verdict was for nine of the 10 deaths. The other, in which the victim was beaten, will be handled in a separate trial.
The serial murders occurred in a 22-month killing spree that ended with Wallace's arrest.

Charlotte police were criticised for not making an arrest sooner. Black residents were particularly critical, saying the police should have realised similarities in the murders -- the victims were young black women who had been strangled. Some were also stabbed.
But police denied charges of racism, responding that Wallace, who is also black, did not fit the general profile of a serial killer -- that of a middle-aged white male who prays on strangers.
